subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sustainable Aviation Fuel usable.

hook.text: A cargo plane runs on fuel made from cooking oil. It emits 80% less CO₂ than regular jet fuel over its lifecycle.

buildup.text: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is made from waste oils, agricultural residues, or synthetic processes.

discovery.text: It's a drop-in replacement—planes use it without engine modifications, blended with conventional fuel.

twist.text: SAF costs 2–4x more than conventional jet fuel. Supply is less than 1% of global aviation fuel demand.

climax.text: Mandates in the EU and US will require SAF blending, driving production scale and cost reduction.

punchline.text: Clean air freight starts with cleaner fuel. SAF is the path.

quiz.question: How much less CO₂ does SAF emit compared to jet fuel?
